title: Unity of Scripture
definition: The unity of Scripture means the many books of the Bible form one coherent divine testimony because one God speaks through them.
summary: Scripture is one unified testimony of God's truth, redemption, and glory.
christFocus: Jesus is the central fulfillment of Scripture's unified message of redemption.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture includes many human authors, genres, historical settings, and time periods, yet it is one unified Word from God. Its message does not collapse into disconnected fragments.

The unity of Scripture is seen in creation, fall, promise, covenant, redemption, kingdom, new creation, and above all in Christ. The Bible tells one grand story of God's glory and saving purpose.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People often read the Bible as disconnected moral lessons or unrelated religious stories. The unity of Scripture matters because it helps believers see God's one redemptive plan centered in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read individual passages as part of the whole Bible. Ask how each text fits God's larger work of creation, fall, redemption, and restoration in Christ.
